audit.reasoning: The classification (tonal; no word-stress rule stated; domain not stated by the source) rests on the language's Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, a 246-pp descriptive grammar (PhD thesis 2003) whose entire phonology chapter we hold as a scan; the tone section was re-read today from the page scan (printed p. 39) and matches the record verbatim, diacritics included; the thesis contents show no stress/accent section and the chapter scanned never mentions stress. Two independent supports are also verbatim in copies we hold (Tezpur 2021 editors: two lexical tones; LSI 1904: stress placement unknown). The only better-dated source, Meitei 2021 (22-pp phonology chapter), is print-only (re-verified: the CFEL PDF is still 12 pp of front matter) and its editors' summary agrees with our classification, so nothing suggests a reclassify. sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III: Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III: Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 398 pp. Purum (Old Kuki group): sketch 'Purum' beginning printed p. 268 (specimens and word list by Babu Bisharup Singh), with Purum also in the Old Kuki comparative introduction.
sources.note: The 1904 Purum sketch, built on written specimens, says plainly that there is no information on tones in this dialect; no tone marks or analysis.
